Fit TWINSPAN and plot its dendrogram using the iPastoralist layout

Source: R/plotClustAggregate_twspn.R
plotClustAggregate_twspn.Rd

Run ecan::twinspan() from scratch on dbClust at every call, using the supplied native fitting parameters. Label surveys with their most abundant species. With aggregate = TRUE, retain every survey, prefix each label with its terminal TWINSPAN group, draw rectangles around groups, and return their dominant species based on mean abundance. This follows the layout of iPastoralist::plotClustAggregate.

Usage

plotClustAggregate_twspn(
  nspePlot = 5,
  firt10 = NULL,
  dbClust = NULL,
  distance = "chord",
  clust.method = "average",
  clust.mar = c(1, 2, 2, 18),
  file.name = "dendrogram.pdf",
  file.height = 30,
  file.width = 15,
  file.res = 200,
  labels.cex = 0.5,
  aggregate = TRUE,
  aggr.Nspe = 5,
  n.clust = NULL,
  save.file = TRUE,
  format = "pdf",
  modified = TRUE,
  n_clusters = NULL,
  cut_levels = c(0, 2, 5, 10, 20),
  min_size = 5,
  max_depth = 6,
  polish = "hill",
  species = FALSE,
  max_indicators = 7,
  diff_threshold = 1/3,
  refine_iter = 5,
  use_indicator = FALSE,
  downweight = TRUE,
  display = !save.file
)

Arguments

nspePlot

Non-negative integer; number of species per survey label.

firt10

Optional data.frame returned by first_ten_species_twspn(). If NULL, compute the ranked species from dbClust. Existing group and order columns are ignored: the new fit determines membership and order. The spelling retains the original argument name.

dbClust

Required numeric surveys-by-species matrix or data.frame. Rows are surveys and columns are species, with unique non-empty names. This exact abundance matrix is used for fitting and group summaries.

distance, clust.method

Retained in their original positions for call compatibility. They are not used by TWINSPAN; use the native fitting arguments below instead.

clust.mar

Four non-negative plot margins passed to graphics::par().

file.name

Output filename, default "dendrogram.pdf". With aggregate = TRUE, save only aggregate_ plus the basename in the same directory, as in the original function. The directory must exist.

file.height, file.width

Positive numeric output dimensions in inches.

file.res

Positive numeric resolution in pixels per inch for PNG.

labels.cex

Positive numeric survey-label size multiplier.

aggregate

Logical; prefix survey labels with their groups, draw group rectangles and return the group-species summary?

aggr.Nspe

Positive integer; number of species in each group summary.

n.clust

Optional compatibility alias for n_clusters. If both are supplied they must be equal. The actual fitted groups determine the rectangles and summaries, even if stopping rules yield fewer groups.

save.file

Logical; export the selected dendrogram to disk?

format

Output format, "pdf" (default) or "png".

modified

Logical; use modified TWINSPAN? Default TRUE.

n_clusters

Optional positive integer; requested number of terminal groups, passed to ecan::twinspan(). NULL leaves the stopping decision to the other native parameters (or uses n.clust, when supplied).

cut_levels

Numeric finite non-negative pseudospecies cut levels.

min_size

Positive integer; minimum group size eligible for division.

max_depth

Non-negative integer; maximum division depth.

polish

Native polishing method, "hill" (default) or "ecan".

species

Logical; also classify species? Default FALSE.

max_indicators

Non-negative integer; maximum indicator pseudospecies.

diff_threshold

Numeric in (0, 1]; native differential-species threshold, used by polish = "ecan".

refine_iter

Non-negative integer; native number of refinement steps, used by polish = "ecan".

use_indicator

Logical; native indicator-ordination option, used by polish = "ecan".

downweight

Logical; downweight rare pseudospecies in the ordination?

display

Logical; also draw the selected dendrogram on the current device? Defaults to !save.file. Set both to FALSE for computation only.

Value

With aggregate = TRUE, a data.frame with group and name, as in the original function. Attributes provide mean.abundance (matrix), n.surveys (named counts), survey.order (survey membership and order), dendrogram (species-labelled tree), aggregate.dendrogram (the same survey tree with group prefixes), and files (saved path). Attributes twinspan, twinspan.parameters and n.clusters contain the newly fitted ecan object, effective native argument values and actual group count. They are also attached to the non-aggregated result. With aggregate = FALSE, invisibly return the species-labelled survey dendrogram, with attributes survey.order and files.

Details

The original plotting arguments are retained. Native TWINSPAN parameters and display are appended after format. No precomputed fitted object is accepted. A single new fit is used for the plain or grouped survey tree, membership, rectangles and mean abundance summaries.

Groups come from the newly fitted object's classification$group. The tree is converted using ecan's own as.hclust.twinspan method, retrieved from its namespace, so the separate package named twinspan cannot intercept the conversion. Branches, order and heights of this new hierarchy are retained. When n_clusters cannot be reached because of min_size, max_depth or a lack of further divisions, the actual fitted groups are used throughout. Heights are reverse division order, not dissimilarities or eigenvalues; zero-height joins within terminal groups are graphical placeholders.

In the aggregated dendrogram, each survey remains a separate leaf. Labels are of the form 0001_Survey | Species abundance | .... Rectangles use dendextend::rect.dendrogram() with k equal to the actual group count, horiz = TRUE, border = 5, lty = 1 and lwd = 1, matching the original function. There is no collapse of surveys into group leaves.

The returned group names follow the original convention: arithmetic mean abundances across all group surveys (including zeros), ranked before rounding, rounded to zero decimal places and formatted as Species (12%). Species with zero means can appear when fewer than aggr.Nspe species have positive means. Ties follow input species order. No percentage conversion is performed: use percentage abundances in dbClust for the % suffix to describe their units correctly.

See also

first_ten_species_twspn(), denspe_twspn(), clustOrder_twspn()

Examples

veg <- rbind(S1 = c(9, 5, 0, 0), S2 = c(8, 4, 1, 0),
             S3 = c(0, 1, 5, 8), S4 = c(0, 0, 4, 7))
colnames(veg) <- c("Species A", "Species B", "Species C", "Species D")
result <- plotClustAggregate_twspn(
  nspePlot = 2, dbClust = veg, modified = TRUE, n_clusters = 2,
  cut_levels = c(0, 2, 5, 10, 20), min_size = 2, max_depth = 6,
  polish = "hill", species = FALSE, save.file = FALSE, display = FALSE
)
result
#>   group                                                           name
#> 1     1 Species D (8%), Species C (4%), Species B (0%), Species A (0%)
#> 2     2 Species A (8%), Species B (4%), Species C (0%), Species D (0%)
attr(result, "mean.abundance")
#>   Species A Species B Species C Species D
#> 1       0.0       0.5       4.5       7.5
#> 2       8.5       4.5       0.5       0.0
fitted <- attr(result, "twinspan")
clustOrder_twspn(fitted)
#>   Survey cluster Survey.order path depth
#> 1     S3       1            1    0     1
#> 2     S4       1            2    0     1
#> 3     S1       2            3    1     1
#> 4     S2       2            4    1     1
